findings.proposed: Keep the text. Flag the row for a rendered RTL check on a ~200 dp row with a long Latin name.
findings.reason: 10 characters of words around the name versus 3 in English. The leading ڈیوائس (6 letters plus a space) costs visible name width. It is still the right choice: list-row.tsx gives this Text no writingDirection, so iOS (NSWritingDirectionNatural) and Android (FIRSTSTRONG_LTR) both take the paragraph base from the first strong character (src/ui/direction.tsx:177-200). The shorter '{device} پر' would start with a Latin name, lay out with an LTR base and put پر on the wrong reading side. Not gating.

observations_not_findings.detail: A device name ending in a neutral ('Pixel!', 'Mac (2)') has that neutral resolved to the RTL embedding direction and drawn on the wrong side of the name. Any catalogue placement has this problem, and policy forbids catalogue bidi controls. Fix at format time by isolating {device} (FSI/PDI or a nested Text). The device-line Text also carries no writingDirection style.
